00012| Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
00013|

00015|

00017|

00029| 
00030| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
00031| 
00032| - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
00033| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
00034| - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
00035|

To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).

Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).

The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

00095| export function extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) {
00096|   if (!output || !output.trim()) {
00097|     return undefined;
00098|   }
00099| 
00100|   // The --format json output contains JSON events, one per line.
00101|   // Filter to only include lines that look like JSON objects.
00102|   const lines = output.split('\n').filter((line) => {
00103|     const trimmed = line.trim();
00104|     return trimmed.startsWith('{') && trimmed.endsWith('}');
00105|   });
00106| 
00107|   if (lines.length === 0) {
00108|     return undefined;
00109|   }
00110| 
00111|   return lines.join('\n');

00114| /**
00115|  * Scrape the OpenCode printed logs for the primary build model.
00116|  * Works on OpenCode <= 1.16.x, whose INFO log lines carry providerID/modelID.
00117|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00118|  *
00119|  * @param {string} output
00120|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00121|  */
00122| export function extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output) {
00123|   let observedModel;
00124| 
00125|   for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
00126|     if (!line.includes('service=llm') || !line.includes('small=false') || !line.includes('agent=build')) {
00127|       continue;
00128|     }
00129| 
00130|     const providerMatch = line.match(/providerID=([^\s]+)/);

00132|     const providerID = providerMatch?.[1];
00133|     const modelID = modelMatch?.[1];

00136|     }

00139|   return observedModel;
00140| }
00141| 
00142| /**
00143|  * Extract the session id from the `--format json` event stream.
00144|  * Every emitted event carries a `sessionID` field.
00145|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00146|  *
00147|  * @param {string|undefined} transcript
00148|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00149|  */
00150| export function extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript) {
00151|   if (!transcript) {
00152|     return undefined;
00153|   }
00154| 
00155|   for (const line of transcript.split('\n')) {
00156|     try {
00157|       const event = JSON.parse(line);
00158|       if (typeof event.sessionID === 'string' && event.sessionID) {
00159|         return event.sessionID;
00160|       }
00161|     } catch {
00162|       // Skip non-JSON lines
00163|     }
00164|   }
00165| 
00166|   return undefined;
00167| }
00168| 
00169| /**
00170|  * Extract the observed model from `opencode export <sessionID>` output.
00171|  * Assistant messages carry `providerID` and `modelID` in their info.
00172|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00173|  *
00174|  * @param {string} exportOutput
00175|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00176|  */
00177| export function extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportOutput) {
00178|   const start = exportOutput.indexOf('{');
00179|   if (start === -1) {
00180|     return undefined;
00181|   }
00182| 
00183|   let parsed;
00184|   try {
00185|     parsed = JSON.parse(exportOutput.slice(start));
00186|   } catch {
00187|     return undefined;
00188|   }
00189| 
00190|   const messages = parsed.messages;
00191|   if (!Array.isArray(messages)) {
00192|     return undefined;
00193|   }
00194| 
00195|   for (const message of messages) {
00196|     const info = message.info;
00197|     if (info?.role !== 'assistant') {
00198|       continue;
00199|     }
00200|     if (
00201|       typeof info.providerID === 'string' && info.providerID &&
00202|       typeof info.modelID === 'string' && info.modelID
00203|     ) {
00204|       return `${info.providerID}/${info.modelID}`;
00205|     }
00206|   }
00207| 
00208|   return undefined;
00209| }
00210| 
00211| /**
00212|  * Run OpenCode over the workspace at `input.cwd` and return a RunnerResult.
00213|  *
00214|  * Auth (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, and OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA when web research is on)
00215|  * arrives via process.env — the orchestrator sets it on the `node run.mjs`
00216|  * invocation, and we pass process.env straight through to the CLI. The runner
00217|  * never handles secrets itself.
00218|  *
00219|  * @param {import('../plugin/contract.js').AgentRunInput} input
00220|  * @returns {Promise<import('../plugin/contract.js').RunnerResult>}
00221|  */
00222| export async function runAgent(input) {
00223|   const args = buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input);
00224| 
00225|   // spawnSync (not a shell string): the prompt is a plain argv element, so there
00226|   // is no shell quoting/escaping to get wrong. Blocking is fine — the runner has
00227|   // nothing else to do while the agent works. The sandbox-level timeout bounds it.
00228|   const res = spawnSync('opencode', args, {
00229|     cwd: input.cwd,
00230|     env: process.env,
00231|     encoding: 'utf8',
00232|     maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00233|   });
00234| 
00235|   const stdout = res.stdout || '';
00236|   const stderr = res.stderr || '';
00237|   // Preserve the old concatenation order: stdout THEN stderr.
00238|   const output = stdout + stderr;
00239|   // spawnSync sets status=null + error when the binary can't be spawned at all.
00240|   const agentExitCode = res.status == null ? -1 : res.status;
00241| 
00242|   // Capture the transcript from the combined output (old: over stdout+stderr).
00243|   const transcript = extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) ?? null;
00244| 
00245|   // Resolve the model OpenCode actually used. The `--format json` events never
00246|   // include it, so first try scraping the printed logs (works on OpenCode <=
00247|   // 1.16.x), then fall back to `opencode export <sessionID>`, whose assistant
00248|   // messages carry providerID/modelID (OpenCode 1.17.0 changed the log format,
00249|   // which broke the scrape). Observation must never fail the run.
00250|   let observedModel = extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output);
00251|   if (!observedModel) {
00252|     const sessionId = extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript ?? undefined);
00253|     if (sessionId) {
00254|       try {
00255|         const exportRes = spawnSync('opencode', ['export', sessionId], {
00256|           cwd: input.cwd,
00257|           env: process.env,
00258|           encoding: 'utf8',
00259|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00260|         });
00261|         if ((exportRes.status == null ? -1 : exportRes.status) === 0) {
00262|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00263|         }
00264|       } catch {
00265|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00266|       }
00267|     }
00268|   }
00269|   const observedModelOrNull = normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) ?? null;
00270| 
00271|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00272|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00273|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00274|     const fallback = res.error
00275|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00276|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;
00277|     return {
00278|       ok: false,
00279|       output,
00280|       transcript,
00281|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00282|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00283|       agentExitCode,
00284|     };
00285|   }
00286| 
00287|   return {
00288|     ok: true,
00289|     output,
00290|     transcript,
00291|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00292|     error: null,
00293|     agentExitCode,
00294|   };
00295| }
00296| 
00297| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00298| 
00299| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00300| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
00301| 
00302| if (isMain) {
00303|   // argv[2] is the AgentRunInput JSON (never contains secrets).
00304|   const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
00305| 
00306|   // Always produce a RunnerResult, even if the runner itself throws, so the host
00307|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00308|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00309|   let result;
00310|   try {
00311|     result = await runAgent(input);
00312|   } catch (e) {
00313|     result = {
00314|       ok: false,
00315|       output: '',
00316|       transcript: null,
00317|       observedModel: null,
00318|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00319|       agentExitCode: -1,
00320|     };
00321|   }
00322| 
00323|   // Source of truth: the result file the host reads back via sandbox.readFile.
00324|   try {
00325|     mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });
00326|     writeFileSync(input.resultPath, JSON.stringify(result));
00327|   } catch {
00328|     // If the file can't be written, the host falls back to the marker line below.
00329|   }
00330| 
00331|   // Fallback channel: a compact status line (no transcript — it can be huge).
00332|   process.stdout.write(
00333|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00334|       JSON.stringify({
00335|         ok: result.ok,
00336|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00337|         error: result.error,
00338|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00339|       }) +
00340|       '\n'
00341|   );
00342| 
00343|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00344|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).

 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

- `lib/products.ts`: added `'use cache'` + `cacheLife('hours')` to `getProduct` and `getRelatedProducts`
- `app/products/[slug]/page.tsx`: added `generateStaticParams` for `lamp`/`vase`, kept the shop frame (`Signal Shop collection`) outside Suspense, and wrapped product details and related products in separate `<Suspense>` boundaries so they stream in while the frame stays visible; currency is read inside the product details boundary so URLs with `?currency=EUR` still render correctly.

Production build succeeded with Partial Prerender for `/products/lamp` and `/products/vase`, no route opt-outs.
